skill.name: frontend-design
skill.description: Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with high design quality. Use this skill for web components, pages, and applications that need polished visual direction and working implementation.
skill.summary: Guides AI agents to build polished frontend interfaces with distinctive visual direction and production-quality implementation.
skill.author: AgentWorkforce

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 7 describes frontend design quality and avoiding generic aesthetics. It does not request host inspection, environment discovery, or system reconnaissance.
Line 33 gives typography guidance for interface design. The text names font choices and contains no instruction to enumerate files, users, networks, or system state.
Line 37 discusses visual background effects such as textures, patterns, shadows, and cursors. This is UI styling guidance, not reconnaissance behavior.

content.value_statement: Generic AI frontends often look similar and lack product-specific character. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward distinctive, working interfaces with stronger typography, layout, motion, and visual detail.
actual_capabilities: Guides selection of a clear aesthetic direction before implementation.
Provides practical guidance for typography, color, motion, layout, and backgrounds.
Encourages working frontend code in HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, Vue, or similar stacks.
Helps avoid generic AI-generated interface patterns and overused visual defaults.
Aligns implementation complexity with the chosen visual concept.
limitations: Does not include starter files, reusable components, or executable scripts.
Does not run tests, accessibility audits, or visual regression checks by itself.
Requires project context, audience details, and technical constraints for best results.
Design guidance may need adaptation for brand rules and accessibility standards.

use_cases.title: Create A Product Page
use_cases.description: Turn a product brief into a memorable frontend page with a clear visual direction and polished implementation details.

use_cases.title: Upgrade A Web Component
use_cases.description: Refine an existing component with stronger typography, spacing, motion, and contextual visual details.

use_cases.title: Prototype A Distinct Interface
use_cases.description: Generate an expressive application screen that explores layout, color, interaction, and visual atmosphere.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Page Build
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you need a single polished page from a short brief.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a distinctive landing page for [product]. Use [framework] and create a complete working interface. Make the visual direction specific to [audience] and avoid generic AI design patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Component Redesign
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when an existing component feels bland or inconsistent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Redesign this [component] for [use case]. Keep the behavior intact, but improve typography, spacing, color, motion, and visual detail so it feels production ready.

prompt_templates.title: Application Screen Concept
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you need a complete interface direction for a product workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a full application screen for [workflow]. Choose a bold but appropriate aesthetic direction, explain the design choices briefly, and implement the interface in [stack].

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Design System Fit
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the design must fit constraints while still feeling distinctive.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a production-quality interface for [product area] using [framework]. Respect these constraints: [brand rules], [accessibility needs], [performance limits], and [responsive targets]. Make the result distinctive without sacrificing usability.

output_examples.input: Create a dashboard for an independent music label that manages releases and artist schedules.
output: A working dashboard interface with an editorial, music-industry visual direction.
Distinct typography, structured release data, schedule views, and polished empty states.
Motion and background details that support the brand without reducing readability.

output_examples.input: Improve a pricing card component for a developer tool website.
output: A redesigned pricing component with clearer hierarchy, stronger contrast, and refined spacing.
Plan comparison states, call-to-action treatments, and responsive behavior.
Visual details that feel specific to developer tooling rather than a generic SaaS template.

output_examples.input: Prototype a mobile onboarding flow for a wellness scheduling app.
output: A mobile-first onboarding sequence with calm visual rhythm and practical form states.
Accessible controls, readable type, and transitions that reinforce progress.
A cohesive interface direction that can guide later screens.

best_practices: Provide the product purpose, audience, brand constraints, and target platform before asking for an interface.
Name the preferred framework, responsive breakpoints, accessibility goals, and performance constraints.
Ask for a brief design rationale when you need to align stakeholders around the visual direction.
anti_patterns: Requesting a generic modern UI without audience, brand, or product context.
Combining many conflicting aesthetics in one prompt without a clear priority.
Treating visual polish as a substitute for accessibility, performance, or working behavior.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create frontend pages, components, and application screens with distinctive visual direction and working implementation.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it generate complete production apps?
faq.answer: It guides production-quality interface work, but complete app delivery still depends on project scope, data, routing, and backend needs.

faq.question: Does it include code files or scripts?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a guidance document and does not include executable scripts or reusable code assets.

faq.question: How should I prompt it for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the product goal, audience, preferred stack, brand constraints, accessibility requirements, and examples of what to avoid.

faq.question: Can it follow an existing design system?
faq.answer: Yes. Include the design system rules and ask the agent to preserve them while improving visual quality and interaction details.
